schema_ddl:
CREATE TABLE PRODUCT (
    PRODUCT_ID INT,
    PRODUCT_NAME VARCHAR(255),
    UNIT_PRICE INT,
    PRIMARY KEY (PRODUCT_ID),
    CHECK (UNIT_PRICE > 0)
);

CREATE TABLE SALES (
    PRODUCT_ID INT,
    SELLER_ID INT,
    BUYER_ID INT,
    SALE_DATE DATE,
    QUANTITY INT,
    PRICE INT,
    FOREIGN KEY (PRODUCT_ID) REFERENCES PRODUCT(PRODUCT_ID),
    CHECK (QUANTITY > 0),
    CHECK (PRICE > 0)
);
q1: SELECT P.PRODUCT_ID, P.PRODUCT_NAME FROM PRODUCT P INNER JOIN ( SELECT PRODUCT_ID FROM SALES GROUP BY PRODUCT_ID HAVING MIN(SALE_DATE) >= '2019-01-01' AND MAX(SALE_DATE) <= '2019-03-31' ) S ON (P.PRODUCT_ID = S.PRODUCT_ID)
q2: SELECT P.PRODUCT_ID, P.PRODUCT_NAME FROM PRODUCT P JOIN ( SELECT DISTINCT PRODUCT_ID FROM SALES GROUP BY PRODUCT_ID HAVING ( MIN(SALE_DATE) >= '2019-01-01' AND MIN(SALE_DATE) <= '2019-03-31' AND MAX(SALE_DATE) >= '2019-01-01' AND MAX(SALE_DATE) <= '2019-03-31' ) ) S ON P.PRODUCT_ID = S.PRODUCT_ID

q2_prompt_sql: SELECT P.PRODUCT_ID, P.PRODUCT_NAME FROM PRODUCT P JOIN ( SELECT DISTINCT PRODUCT_ID FROM SALES GROUP BY PRODUCT_ID HAVING ( MIN(SALE_DATE) >= '2019-01-01' AND MIN(SALE_DATE) <= '2019-03-31' AND MAX(SALE_DATE) >= '2019-01-01' AND MAX(SALE_DATE) <= '2019-03-31' ) ) S ON P.PRODUCT_ID = S.PRODUCT_ID
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent. Q1 filters products whose all sales occurred within the date range '2019-01-01' to '2019-03-31' by checking that both MIN(SALE_DATE) and MAX(SALE_DATE) fall within that range. Q2 uses MIN(SALE_DATE) and MAX(SALE_DATE) in a different logical combination that does not enforce the same condition correctly, potentially allowing sales outside the range.
counterexample_dsp: A product with one sale on '2018-12-31' and another on '2019-04-01' will be excluded by Q1 but may be included by Q2 due to incorrect HAVING logic in Q2.
